brief:
The death of Mahmoud Muhammad Arabi Mohsen, who carried out a stabbing operation near Osarin village south of Nablus, has revived attention to his grandfather's role in Palestinian resistance, according to Shehab Wire. Resistance fighter Arabi Badawi was among the men who accompanied Sheikh Izz al-Din al-Qassam and participated in armed activities during the British Mandate period in Palestine.

The case illustrates a generational continuum in Palestinian armed resistance, connecting the younger Mohsen's actions to family involvement in anti-colonial struggle that stretched across decades. His grandfather's activities under the mandate represent an earlier phase of organized Palestinian resistance before the establishment of Israel in 1948.
